title: Adaptive Business Discovery Question Bank

questions.question: What does your business do, and who does it serve?
questions.why: Establishes the business and audience context.

questions.question: What are the main products or services the website should represent?
questions.why: Defines the offering that the website must communicate.

questions.question: Which markets, regions, or customer segments are in scope?
questions.why: May affect content, localization, operations, and applicable requirements.

questions.question: What prompted this website project now?
questions.why: Identifies the underlying trigger and business problem.

questions.question: What should improve after the project is completed?
How do you currently measure this outcome, if at all?
Is this a new website, a redesign, a rebuild, or a migration?
Which current pages, content, features, and workflows must be preserved?
questions.why: Prevents accidental loss of existing functionality.

questions.question: Which existing platforms and systems does the website depend on?
Who will use the website, and what should each group be able to accomplish?
questions.why: Establishes user groups and intended tasks.

questions.question: What are the most important tasks users must complete?
questions.why: Identifies key journeys and functional requirements.

questions.question: Which tasks currently require manual staff intervention or another system?
Are there fixed deadlines, budget limits, or launch dependencies?
Are there technology, vendor, hosting, or platform requirements?
Are there privacy, security, accessibility, or legal requirements that must be reviewed?
questions.why: Identifies risks and required specialist involvement.

questions.question: Who approves the scope, content, design, integrations, and final launch?
What would make this project unsuccessful, even if the website looks good?
questions.why: Surfaces failure conditions and hidden expectations.

questions.question: Who will own website content, maintenance, and performance after launch?

adaptive_question_rules: Ask one focused question at a time in conversational discovery unless grouping questions is clearly more efficient.
Do not ask for information already established by reliable evidence.
Ask conditional questions only when the condition applies.
Prioritize questions that could change scope, architecture, cost, risk, or approval requirements.
Explain why a question matters when the reason may not be obvious.
Allow noncritical answers to remain unknown during early discovery.
When the customer cannot answer a technical question, identify the relevant person or evidence needed.
